findings.checklist_item: Specify, for the step-4 def-count fallback, how re-inlined duplication (a copy that never calls the one def) is prevented — e.g. require that such constructs instead expose at least one distinctive atom to scan for, or state why a construct with genuinely no distinctive atoms cannot be re-inlined.
evidence: Step 4: 'Where the construct has no distinctive atoms, assert the definition count of the named symbol instead (exactly one def <name> under src/rebar).'
Context: 'every hotspot is the same decision written in two to seven places' — duplication is by imitation/inlining, not only by re-defining a function
A def-count guard passes even if a caller re-inlines the body and never calls the one def
findings.finding: The step-4 fallback guard ('assert the definition count of the named symbol ... exactly one `def <name>` under src/rebar') pins only the DEFINITION count and does not catch a duplicated computation that is re-inlined by copy-paste without calling the shared symbol — yet the plan's own premise is 'the same decision written in two to seven places', which includes inline re-implementations that carry no `def`.
scenarios: A child whose construct 'has no distinctive atoms' uses the def-count fallback; a later site copies the logic inline (no new def, no call to the symbol); the guard stays green and the divergence class the review documents re-enters.
